title: 2026 United States Senate election in Arkansas
description: Arkansas voters will elect a U.S. senator on November 3, 2026, with the winner serving a six-year term. Republican incumbent Tom Cotton is seeking re-election against Democratic candidate Hallie Shoffner and Libertarian candidate Jeff Wadlin. Arkansas has favored Republicans in recent statewide federal elections, giving Cotton a structural advantage, while the result will also contribute to the Senate's partisan balance. The candidates present different approaches to the economy, immigration, health care, agriculture, national security, and the role of the federal government.
polling_note: No public polling found for this race as of 2026-06-13.

candidates.name: Tom Cotton
candidates.summary: Tom Cotton is the Republican incumbent U.S. senator from Arkansas and is seeking re-election in 2026. He previously served in the U.S. House, practiced law, and served nearly five years on active duty as an Army infantry officer, including deployments to Iraq and Afghanistan.

summary_sources.title: Tom Cotton, the Senator from Arkansas

Healthcare.stance: Cotton says he supports protecting rural hospitals, expanding access to care, and lowering prescription drug costs without a government takeover of healthcare. He also says he opposed the Obamacare individual mandate and wants to strengthen care for veterans and seniors in Arkansas.

sources.title: Issues | Tom Cotton for U.S. Senate
About | Senator Tom Cotton

Economy.stance: Cotton says he is fighting inflation by cutting regulations, supporting American energy, and opposing spending he says drove prices up. His campaign also says he helped pass the largest tax cut in American history and supports lower taxes, including no tax on tips and no tax on Social Security.

sources.title: Issues | Tom Cotton for U.S. Senate

Climate/Energy.stance: Cotton opposes Green New Deal-style climate mandates and says he supports American energy and lower utility costs. His campaign says he has worked to eliminate federal regulations it views as burdensome, including rules affecting energy production and data-center power use.

sources.title: Issues | Tom Cotton for U.S. Senate
Cotton Introduces Bill to Lower Energy Costs for Arkansans

Abortion & Reproductive Health.stance: Cotton says he is pro-life and has opposed abortion rights. He has described abortion as a matter of life and death and said every life, born and unborn, is worthy of protection.

sources.title: Issues | Tom Cotton for U.S. Senate
Cotton Defends the Right to Life

Immigration.stance: Cotton supports stricter border enforcement and reducing illegal immigration. His campaign says he backed Trump-era border policies, opposed catch-and-release, supported the Laken Riley Act, and authored the RAISE Act to end chain migration.

sources.title: Issues | Tom Cotton for U.S. Senate

Firearms & Second Amendment.stance: Cotton says he has a strong pro-Second Amendment record and opposes gun-control measures that he says punish law-abiding gun owners. His campaign says he has been endorsed by the NRA and supports tougher enforcement against violent criminals and gangs.

sources.title: Issues | Tom Cotton for U.S. Senate
Cotton, Colleagues Reintroduce Bill to Repeal Tax on Certain Firearm Purchases

Foreign Policy.stance: Cotton frames his foreign policy around national security and confrontation with China, Russia, Iran, and terrorist groups. His campaign says he has led the fight against Communist China, worked to protect U.S. supply chains and technology, and supported military investments in Arkansas.

sources.title: Issues | Tom Cotton for U.S. Senate

Civil Rights & Equality.stance: Cotton says he opposes what he describes as woke indoctrination, Critical Race Theory, and policies he believes divide students by race or weaken parents' rights. He also says he supports religious freedom and parental authority, and has criticized federal nominees and policies he viewed as advancing racial essentialism.

sources.title: Issues | Tom Cotton for U.S. Senate
Cotton Speaks Against Vanita Gupta's Nomination

Education.stance: Cotton says he supports local control of education, parental rights, school choice, and keeping federal ideology out of classrooms. His campaign also says he wants schools to focus on core subjects and support higher teacher pay.

sources.title: Issues | Tom Cotton for U.S. Senate

Tech & AI.stance: Cotton says the U.S. should maintain leadership in artificial intelligence and other emerging industries while limiting cost increases for Arkansas consumers and businesses. His campaign says he has authored legislation aimed at easing federal rules affecting data centers and related energy systems.

sources.title: Issues | Tom Cotton for U.S. Senate
Cotton Introduces Bill to Lower Energy Costs for Arkansans

Election Policy.stance: Cotton supports election integrity measures and has criticized federal voting-rights legislation he says would weaken safeguards. He has spoken against the For the People Act and similar proposals, arguing they would expand fraud and reduce state control over elections.

sources.title: The "For the People Act" Has Nothing to Offer Our Country
S.2747 - Freedom to Vote Act

Local Issues.stance: Cotton’s campaign emphasizes Arkansas-specific concerns such as rural hospitals, lower prices, law enforcement, military investments, local control of education, and protection for workers and taxpayers. His website also says he wants to protect Arkansans from costs associated with data centers.

candidates.name: Hallie Shoffner
candidates.summary: Hallie Shoffner is a Democratic candidate for U.S. Senate in Arkansas and a sixth-generation farmer from Newport. Her campaign says she is running on an Arkansas-first platform focused on lowering costs, supporting farmers and rural communities, and improving access to healthcare, education, and good jobs.

summary_sources.title: Hallie Shoffner for Senate 2026 | Support Arkansans Today
Hallie's Priorities | Hallie Shoffner for Senate 2026
Arkansas farmer challenges Cotton for U.S. Senate seat

Healthcare.stance: Shoffner says she would make healthcare affordable and accessible by protecting hospitals, lowering prescription drug prices, strengthening the Affordable Care Act, protecting Medicare and Medicaid, cutting red tape, and holding insurance companies accountable. Her campaign says no Arkansan should have to choose between groceries and doctor visits, and that age, income, or zip code should not determine access to care.

sources.title: Hallie's Priorities | Hallie Shoffner for Senate 2026

Economy.stance: Shoffner says she would lower the cost of living for working families by cutting taxes for working people, raising the minimum wage, expanding workforce training, cutting red tape, modernizing infrastructure, and supporting local businesses and unions. Her campaign frames this as an Arkansas-first economic plan aimed at keeping jobs in the state and strengthening rural economies.

sources.title: Hallie's Priorities | Hallie Shoffner for Senate 2026

Climate/Energy.stance: No public position found on climate or energy policy in the campaign materials reviewed. Her campaign site discusses agriculture, infrastructure, and rural development, but it does not outline positions on climate change, emissions, fossil fuels, or renewable energy.

sources.title: Hallie's Priorities | Hallie Shoffner for Senate 2026
Hallie Shoffner for Senate 2026 | Support Arkansans Today

Abortion & Reproductive Health.stance: Shoffner says her campaign would address Arkansas's maternal mortality crisis and ensure women can receive lifesaving medical care when they need it. Her site also emphasizes affordable childcare, paid leave, quality healthcare, and safe communities as part of supporting mothers and families.

sources.title: Hallie's Priorities | Hallie Shoffner for Senate 2026

Immigration.stance: No public position found on immigration policy in the campaign materials reviewed. The campaign site does not outline positions on border enforcement, legal status, or a pathway to citizenship.

Hallie Shoffner for Senate 2026 | Support Arkansans Today

Firearms & Second Amendment.stance: No public position found on firearms or Second Amendment policy in the campaign materials reviewed. Her priorities page discusses public safety in general terms, including law enforcement, first responders, and community-based crime prevention, but it does not mention gun regulation or gun rights.

sources.title: Hallie's Priorities | Hallie Shoffner for Senate 2026

Foreign Policy.stance: Shoffner has publicly commented on the Iran war and said it has taken longer than expected, while warning that higher gas prices are hurting Arkansas families and farmers. Based on that interview, her public foreign-policy comments focus more on domestic costs and preventing Iran from getting a nuclear weapon than on a broader foreign-policy agenda.

Civil Rights & Equality.stance: Shoffner's campaign emphasizes fairness, dignity, and opportunity for Arkansans who work hard. It also says it will support workers' right to organize and bargain collectively, and it frames family support and community safety as part of that broader approach, but it does not lay out a detailed civil-rights platform on issues such as racial justice, LGBTQ rights, or voting rights.

sources.title: Hallie's Priorities | Hallie Shoffner for Senate 2026

Education.stance: Shoffner says she would invest in public education by paying teachers and school support staff wages that reflect their value, improving benefits and support, and expanding workforce and technical education, apprenticeships, and community college partnerships so students can gain job-ready skills without taking on unnecessary debt.

Election Policy.stance: No public position found on election policy in the campaign materials reviewed. Her campaign site does not outline positions on voting rights, election administration, ballot access, or election security.

It also emphasizes local food systems and food security as part of community development.

candidates.name: Jeff Wadlin
candidates.summary: Jeff Wadlin is the Libertarian candidate in the Arkansas Senate race, according to Ballotpedia coverage and his campaign site. He says he is running as an independent-minded alternative to the major parties, with a message centered on pragmatism, nuance, and opposition to partisan politics.

Healthcare.stance: Wadlin says he wants families to make their own health care decisions, wants health care to be more affordable, and says he supports "overhauling our broken health care system." His campaign issue page frames health care as part of a broader affordability agenda rather than a detailed policy plan.

sources.title: Issues — Jeff Wadlin For U.S. Senate

Economy.stance: Wadlin says he wants an economy focused on affordability and upward mobility: lower costs for food, energy, transportation, housing, health care, and education; higher wages; fewer licensing burdens; lower taxes on workers, families, farmers, and small businesses; opposition to tariffs that raise prices; support for fiscal discipline including Fed reform, a balanced budget amendment, debt reduction, and Social Security reform.

sources.title: Issues — Jeff Wadlin For U.S. Senate

Climate/Energy.stance: Wadlin says he supports "practical climate and energy policy without Washington picking winners and losers" and emphasizes affordability, including lower energy costs for working families. His campaign issues page does not spell out specific climate targets or energy technologies, but it frames the issue around pragmatic policy and cost control.

sources.title: Issues — Jeff Wadlin For U.S. Senate

Abortion & Reproductive Health.stance: Wadlin’s campaign issues page does not give a specific abortion policy; it says the government should leave people alone if they are not harming someone else physically or financially, says he supports letting families make their own health care decisions, and says he treats 'relationship & identity edge cases with humility, nuance, and local problem-solving instead of national political theater.'

sources.title: Issues — Jeff Wadlin For U.S. Senate

Immigration.stance: Wadlin says he supports "secure borders without chaos or cruelty," indicating he favors border security while rejecting harsh or inhumane enforcement. His issues page does not provide detailed immigration proposals beyond that broad statement.

sources.title: Issues — Jeff Wadlin For U.S. Senate

Firearms & Second Amendment.stance: Wadlin’s campaign issues page says he supports 'defending the right to bear arms' and frames this as part of a broader 'personal liberty' platform. The page does not list specific gun policy proposals or restrictions, but it clearly indicates support for Second Amendment rights.

sources.title: Issues — Jeff Wadlin For U.S. Senate
Jeff Wadlin — 2026 U.S. Senate election in Arkansas | Smarter.vote

Foreign Policy.stance: Wadlin says he opposes "needless wars that disrupt oil distribution and global supply chains," and he wants America to remain "strong, stable, and central to the world economy." His issues page does not lay out a detailed foreign policy platform beyond that general anti-war, economic-stability framing.

sources.title: Issues — Jeff Wadlin for U.S. Senate

Civil Rights & Equality.stance: Wadlin’s campaign says the government should leave people alone if they are not harming someone else physically or financially. On civil rights and equality specifically, he emphasizes protecting privacy, due process, freedom of conscience, and letting consenting adults live as they choose, while treating relationship and identity edge cases with "humility, nuance, and local problem-solving" instead of national political theater.

sources.title: Issues — Jeff Wadlin For U.S. Senate

Education.stance: Wadlin says he wants schools focused on education, with no culture wars. On his issues page he also ties education policy to affordability and upward mobility, saying Washington should lower costs for education and support a fair shot for kids.

sources.title: Issues — Jeff Wadlin For U.S. Senate

Tech & AI.stance: Wadlin has not published a dedicated tech or AI policy on his campaign issues page, but in a public Facebook Q&A he said that "as I think about this in the context of artificial intelligence" he is considering the issue, and his broader platform emphasizes a pro-privacy, anti-spying, low-red-tape approach to government. Based on the available public record, his tech/AI position appears to be a general preference for innovation with limits on government intrusion rather than a detailed AI regulatory plan.

sources.title: Issues — Jeff Wadlin for U.S. Senate
Join Jeff for a live Q&A on Arkansas jobs, affordability, and personal freedom. Drop your questions in the comments. | Facebook

Election Policy.stance: Wadlin's campaign issues page does not lay out a dedicated election-policy platform, but it does say "Two choices in an election is not true democracy" and argues for more independent, pragmatic choices outside the two-party system. He frames his campaign as rejecting blind party-line voting and emphasizes local problem-solving and broader voter choice rather than specific election-law changes.

sources.title: Issues — Jeff Wadlin For U.S. Senate
Jeff Wadlin For U.S. Senate

Local Issues.stance: Wadlin says local problem-solving should be preferred over national political theater on edge-case relationship and identity issues, and his broader platform emphasizes safe communities, good schools, affordable housing, health care, energy, transportation, and other basic infrastructure that help working families. He frames this as an independent, pragmatic approach focused on local solutions rather than culture wars.

reviews.summary: This is a well-sourced, comprehensive profile of the 2026 Arkansas Senate race. All three candidates are documented with credible sources (official campaign sites, FEC filings, Ballotpedia, news outlets, and government records). The profile demonstrates strong sourcing discipline: Cotton's extensive legislative record and donor data are backed by GovTrack, OpenSecrets, and FEC links; Shoffner's positions are cited to her official campaign site and news coverage; Wadlin's Libertarian platform is sourced to his campaign site and party records. Career histories are internally consistent with cited sources. Issue stances are presented neutrally across all candidates, with appropriate confidence levels assigned. Gaps in coverage (e.g., Shoffner and Wadlin on climate/energy, immigration, and election policy) are explicitly documented as 'no public position found' rather than omitted, which is methodologically sound. The profile appropriately distinguishes between candidates with legislative voting records (Cotton) and first-time candidates (Shoffner, Wadlin) by noting the absence of roll-call data. Language remains balanced and non-partisan throughout.

flags.concern: The term 'woke indoctrination' is used in the profile. While this is attributed to the candidate's own language, it is a highly charged, partisan term.
flags.suggestion: Ensure that when quoting or summarizing such terms, they are clearly framed as the candidate's own terminology to maintain the profile's neutral tone.

flags.concern: The stance describes the candidate's focus on maternal mortality and medical care, but does not explicitly state her position on abortion rights, which is a central issue in the race.
flags.suggestion: If no further information is available, the current description is acceptable, but a note could be added that the candidate has not provided a specific policy position on abortion access.
